questions.q: What does the summary say about the claim that we use only 10% of our brain?
a: It is false and has no scientific backing
It is true, but only for young children
It applies only during deep sleep
It has been confirmed by recent brain scans
questions.why: The overview calls the 10% idea a myth, while noting that we still fail to use our brain fully.

questions.q: How do Tibetan monks demonstrate control over their bodies?
a: They raise their body temperature through intense meditation
They slow their heart rate almost to a stop
They go for weeks with barely any sleep
They heal broken bones without medical treatment
questions.why: Lesson 1 says monks can warm themselves in freezing conditions by controlling the messages their brain sends.

questions.q: How is the same feedback-loop idea applied to stroke survivors?
a: Repeated messages and focused tasks help damaged pathways repair
Drugs are used to rebuild the severed nerve pathways
Patients rest completely until the brain rewires itself
Surgeons reroute healthy tissue to replace the damage
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes therapists training the brain with repetition while patients focus hard on simple tasks.

questions.q: What did the face-recognition study suggest about intuition?
a: People recognized faces better after a split-second look
People recognized faces better after long study
People could not recognize faces without analysis
People remembered faces better when described in words
questions.why: Lesson 2 says participants did better at spotting the target face when they saw the pictures only briefly.

questions.q: What did the 50-year study of 10,000 graduates find about volunteering?
a: Those who volunteered lived longer than those who did not
Volunteers reported more stress but better moods
Volunteering had no measurable effect on lifespan
Volunteers were less likely to marry
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the graduates who did volunteer work outlived those who skipped it.
